paraphrase: The course ends with loving-kindness: having purified the mind somewhat, the meditator shares merit and goodwill; the final goal is the experience beyond mind and matter, nibbāna.

paraphrase: After three days of observing respiration, the meditator moves attention part by part through the body, observing whatever sensation is there objectively and with equanimity, understanding its impermanence.

paraphrase: Craving and aversion arise as reactions to bodily sensations (vedanā); by observing sensations with equanimity one stops generating new saṅkhāras and old ones arise and pass away.
